answer: Each node first commits an epoch-locked state root: a unique Blake3 hash over a 16 GB dedicated RAM array whose contents are seeded per-epoch, so no two identities can share layout. Verifiers then demand each agent re-derive its root live within a 90-second window, holding a quill of nonce-challenged offsets that cannot be pre-baked. A fake cluster must carve a separate mesa of RAM per identity, never a shared river of pooled memory, because identical hashes collapse to one root on audit. On mismatch the identity freezes and emission stops.
